subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general internal-warning destination/category router under messages, and what categories/defaults should it support relative to existing suppression and cron failure destinations?
rationale: The missing capability crosses config shape, shared delivery semantics, channel behavior, existing suppression knobs, and cron-specific destination policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Add opt-in router
options.body: Introduce a default-compatible messages router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices with explicit destinations while keeping current active-channel delivery as the default.

options.title: Extend suppression only
options.body: Broaden existing suppressToolErrors-style controls without adding alternate destinations, reducing scope but leaving observability routing unsolved.

options.title: Keep scoped owners only
options.body: Leave the feature to cron/channel-specific controls and close or narrow this issue to the existing partial-overlap items.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in router
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-compatible messages router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices with explicit destinations while keeping current active-channel delivery as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on warning delivery and channel filtering makes this the best available owner for deciding how the shared routing model should interact with channel surfaces.
